entries.title: Research@ 2026: Novel capabilities and intelligence
entries.summary: An animated collage showing research-focusing images on a black background
entries.content:
Technology is supercharging scientific discovery and improving people's lives. At Google Research, we’re pioneering breakthroughs across domains and bringing our research to reality to benefit people everywhere.

Today at Research@ in Mountain View, we’re sharing our latest milestones and some of the advanced AI capabilities and intelligence that we’re putting in the hands of experts. Our latest breakthroughs help drive progress on the world’s most pressing challenges including healthcare, crisis resilience, and beyond. This momentum builds on our recent announcements from AMIE in the clinic, to Earth AI for public health, to Project Suncatcher in orbit.

entries.title: Guide your campaign spending with new priority and allocation features
entries.content:
Marketers want more transparency into their ad campaigns and choice over how they direct their ad budgets. Building on updates like Smart Bidding Exploration and campaign total budgets, which put more control into the hands of advertisers, we’re introducing new optional controls in Google Ads: channel prioritization and budget allocation. As these controls roll out globally across Search, Shopping, Performance Max, and Demand Gen, marketers will have even greater flexibility deciding where their budgets flow across Google inventory and partner networks, like Search partners and the Google Display Network.

Choose which channels get funded first

Channel prioritization lets marketers decide where their budgets go first by categorizing inventory as “High priority” or “Low priority” for specific channels or channel groupings. When configured, campaigns will fully fund high-priority channels (within their target when using Target CPA or Target ROAS) before allocating the remaining budget to lower-priority channels. For example, on Search campaigns, marketers can now set Google Search, Search partners, and Google Display Network into different priority levels depending on what they value. In Performance Max and Demand Gen campaigns, Google surfaces like Search, YouTube, Maps, Gmail, and Discover are prioritized together as "Google channels.”

These controls are rolling out at the account and campaign levels, and also apply to shared budgets. Distinct priority tiers can be set across Search, Shopping, Performance Max, and Demand Gen campaign types.

Set spending limits with flexible budget allocation

With this update, we’re also introducing more flexible budget allocation controls at the channel level. When a channel or channel grouping is set as "Low priority," advertisers will be able to specify a maximum percentage of their daily budget to stay within their desired boundaries on those channels. On a best-effort basis, our tools will aim to keep spend on those channels within that limit. This is particularly helpful for campaigns with Target CPA or Target ROAS bidding that are not limited by budget since channel prioritization alone will generally not have an impact there.

These features give marketers more control than all-or-nothing opt-outs. Marketers who have historically opted out of Search partners and the Google Display Network can use this new lever to test these networks with more confidence and clearer limits, rather than turning them off entirely. Marketers who have campaigns currently running on Search partners or the Google Display Network have the option to set a budget allocation should they choose.

Starting in February 2027, for Search campaigns with the Google Display Network turned on, the current spend allocation setup will go away, and advertisers may see a shift in channel spending. To keep their current configuration, they can set the Google Display Network to “Low priority” with a 50% budget allocation.

These optional features are rolling out to Search, Shopping, Performance Max, and Demand Gen over the next months. With these new controls in place, marketers can confidently spend as the holidays approach and meet demand during the peak season. Learn more in our Help Center.

entries.title: Check out this year’s buzziest Halloween trends.
entries.summary: Ready or not, spooky season is here. To help you prepare, we’re launching Google Frightgeist, our annual interactive website highlighting the top trending searches for H…
entries.content:
Ready or not, spooky season is here. To help you prepare, we’re launching Google Frightgeist, our annual interactive website highlighting the top trending searches for Halloween costumes, movies, and more.

Here’s a peek at what’s trending in 2026:

  • Costumes: Horror movie characters, TV and movie favorites, country legends, and some out-of-the-box ideas (stress balls?!) top the charts.
  • Party essentials: “Witches brew punch” is the top trending Halloween drink, and search interest in “cauldron crock pot” is at an all-time high.
  • Spooky effects: “How to make a bubbling cauldron” is a breakout search this month, and “where can I buy dry ice,” which spikes every year, is among the top “where can I buy” Halloween searches.
  • Scary watchlists: Searches for "nostalgic halloween movies" have increased year-over-year since 2019. “Gothic horror movies” and “mascot horror movies” are this year’s top trending horror movie searches.

Explore the full list of Halloween trends here.

entries.title: 6 ways to trick-or-treat yourself to the ultimate Halloween with Search
entries.summary: An abandoned video rental store lit by a red neon sign at night.
entries.content:
Whether your spooky spirit awakens on October 1 or you’re scrambling for a low-effort costume an hour before a party, Halloween prep shouldn’t feel like a curse.

No matter how you celebrate, hunting down the perfect costume and brewing up ideas for an epic party don’t have to drain your time — or your wallet. Here are six ways that Search can work its magic and do the heavy lifting this season.

1. Get costume inspo.

Check out Google’s annual Frightgeist site for outfit inspiration. You can explore the top trending costumes nationwide and even see what’s trending in your neighborhood.

2. Turn your closet into a costume.

Whether you’ve waited until the last minute or just don’t want to spend money on a costume this year, Lens in Search can tell you how to use things from your closet to create the perfect Halloween ensemble. Simply lay out a few items from your wardrobe, take a picture, and ask something like, “Help me come up with ideas to DIY a Halloween costume using these statement pieces from my closet.”

3. Figure out your Halloween makeup.

Before you break out the face paint, visualize the look with image generation in Search. Open the Google app for Android or iOS, tap the Lens camera icon in the search bar, and then select “Create” at the bottom of your screen. Then take a selfie and add something like, “I want to do unicorn makeup for Halloween. Show me what I could do that will stand out at a party without being too hard to replicate.” This way, you can generate a preview of the look and, if you like it, you can follow up to figure out what products you need to pull it off.

4. Find free activities near you.

If you’re looking for ways to do Halloween on a budget, ask AI Mode in Search for help finding free activities and events in your neighborhood. It can help identify nearby costume swaps, community and neighborhood festivals, creative workshops and more!

5. Build a spooky soundtrack.

Want to set the mood for your Halloween party but don’t want to spend hours creating a playlist? Connect your YouTube Music account with Search, and ask AI Mode to “Make a spooky background playlist for a Halloween party that moves from eerie ambient synth at dinner to upbeat retro horror-funk for when the party gets going.”

6. Create a scary movie watchlist.

If you prefer to celebrate Halloween with a movie marathon but don’t know what to watch, use AI Mode to come up with a hyper-specific list of movies. Try asking something like, “Help me make a 90s nostalgia Halloween movie watchlist. I like witchy aesthetics, small-town autumn settings, and practical effects but without heavy gore" to quickly narrow down your options to a list that matches your vibe.

entries.title: 17 organizations using AI to accelerate scientific breakthroughs
entries.summary: Two photos of women looking at tablets, one in a field and one in a lab, with curved lines running through the image
entries.content:
We’re standing at a profound inflection point in scientific discovery. AI is ushering in a new era of scientific research, from unraveling the complexities of human disease to forecasting environmental shifts. This work aims to tackle global challenges faster and more effectively than ever before, improving lives everywhere.

Earlier this year, we launched the Google.org Impact Challenge: AI for Science, an open call to organizations harnessing AI for scientific breakthroughs. We received applications across 30 countries, in fields like climate, health, and foundational science.

Today, we’re announcing the 17 selected recipient organizations, which will receive a total of $36 million in funding. Organizations can choose to participate in a six-month Google.org Accelerator, where they will receive engineering support, technical mentorship, and Google infrastructure to transform their ideas into scaled solutions. From advanced energy approaches to decoding the brain, these organizations are pushing the boundaries of scientific discovery for societal impact.

Climate resilience and environmental science

  • AfriClimate AI Limited is decoding the atmospheric precursors of deadly storm systems across Africa, aiming to extend flash-flood warning times from under three hours to over six hours.
  • Inria Chile Research Center is building a multimodal world foundation model of the ocean by creating a digital twin of Earth's marine ecosystems.
  • Massachusetts Institute of Technology is accelerating automated materials discovery by training AI agents to autonomously interpret experimental microscopic imagery.
  • Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics in partnership with TU Eindhoven, is bridging the simulation-to-reality gap for clean fusion energy by using physics-informed AI to model chaotic conditions inside fusion reactors.
  • The University of Texas at Austin is developing neural network models to accelerate the design of compact fusion reactors.
  • UC San Diego is pioneering an agentic AI pipeline that discovers interpretable climate physics from Earth observations, builds a next-generation climate model, and decides where to collect new ocean observations.
  • University of Cambridge is accelerating the development of durable sodium-ion batteries by combining physics foundation models and microscopy to forecast cathode degradation.
  • University of Washington is designing proteins with natural language to advance sustainability applications, such as plastic degradation.

Health and life sciences

  • AITHYRA Research Institute, in collaboration with EPFL, is uncovering how viruses manipulate cells and creating an AI-designed protein library to discover therapeutics for undruggable proteins.
  • Allen Institute is designing DNA sequences that reach brain cell types more vulnerable to neurodegenerative diseases, openly sharing every model, sequence, and result.
  • Australian National University is leading an international collaboration to end trial-and-error chemotherapy and advance equitable precision oncology.
  • National University of Singapore is predicting disease impacts by mapping how genetic variants regulate RNA splicing at a population scale.
  • New York University Grossman School of Medicine is working to uncover unknown causes of mutations by detecting diverse types of DNA damage using AI.
  • University of California, Berkeley is turning black-box predictions into clear clinical biomarkers by extracting interpretable hypotheses from medical AI models.
  • The University of Cape Town (UCT) is developing an AI-powered platform to map genetic variation in African drug-metabolizing genes, helping guide clinical drug choices and improve treatment safety.
  • University of Pittsburgh is identifying genetic switches to accelerate new cardiac therapies using a novel geometric AI model to compare heart regeneration across species.
  • University of Toronto is enabling computer-guided therapeutic drug design by mapping the design space for peptide-based drugs with an AI foundation model.

These organizations represent an exciting range of ideas, disciplines, and approaches to some of the world’s most pressing challenges. We look forward to supporting their work and to seeing what becomes possible when scientific expertise and AI come together to tackle challenges that affect us all.

entries.title: We’re powering European scientific discovery with advanced AI compute and frontier models.
entries.summary: Photo of Grand Canal Dock, Dublin City Centre, Ireland
entries.content:
Google DeepMind and Google Cloud are providing up to 200 top European scientific researchers with direct access to our frontier models, together with $3 million in compute credits.

Through this pledge, researchers will gain direct access to our leading scientific tools including AlphaFold 3, WeatherNext, AlphaGenome, AlphaEvolve, and AlphaEarth Foundations.

This commitment supports the European Union’s AI for Science work by making some of our frontier models available via the RAISE initiative, which seeks to help bridge the compute gap European scientists sometimes face.

By delivering vital compute power and state-of-the-art tools directly to research teams, this effort aims to accelerate the pace of European innovation and reinforce the continent's scientific competitiveness.

Researchers will be equipped to tackle complex challenges faster, from predicting extreme weather patterns to mapping molecular structures, ensuring that European science remains vibrant and at the forefront of discovery.

entries.title: Enabling an AI-first European economy
entries.summary: A collage of five photos showcasing professionals and researchers who utilize AI and are featured in the Economic Impact Report. The five images are in settings such as automotive manufacturing, laboratory science, app based learning, skincare production
entries.content:
In County Clare, Ireland, entrepreneur Danilly Carvalho has built something truly special. She’s the founder of IPERA, a skincare brand that’s scaling from the west of Ireland to the world. After joining a skills training program, Danilly used Gemini to analyze complex international consumer trends and completely rebrand her business. Within a year, online sales surged by 45%, and her “local” business expanded into seven countries.

This is just one example of the massive economic potential of this moment. The European Union is one of the world’s largest and most digitally connected economic areas. Across Europe, our partners are turning the potential of AI into measurable progress.

Breaking down our economic impact

To understand the scale of what we can achieve together, today we're releasing Google’s 2025 EU Economic Impact Report, commissioned by Google and developed by Implement Consulting Group. The report shows how Google’s products and platforms, investments in infrastructure, and Cloud and AI technologies contributed more than €200 billion to EU GDP. That’s about 1% of total EU GDP, approaching the contribution of the entire EU agriculture sector.

This impact is broken down across three areas:

  • Products and platforms (approx €157 billion): Tools like Search, Ads, Android, Google Play, Chrome, and YouTube connect millions of European businesses to global markets, allow creators to monetize content, and help citizens access essential information and services.
  • AI and Cloud (approx €32 billion): Cloud services and artificial intelligence help European enterprises, public institutions, and developers scale infrastructure, optimize operations, and build new capabilities securely within Europe.
  • Infrastructure and offices (approx €11B): Our data centers, offices and operations generate direct economic value through local procurement, supply-chain partnerships, and community investments.

Productivity gains

AI productivity gains aren't hypothetical; they're happening across the continent right now. Recent findings by the European Investment Bank show AI is helping to lift labor productivity by an average of 4% across adopting firms without displacing employment.

Take Renault Group. Amidst the rising costs and production pressures of today’s automotive sector, Renault Group is using Google AI to modernize its manufacturing operations and secure their competitiveness. On the factory floor, AI is preventing breakdowns and detecting manufacturing defects in real time, cutting factory downtime and production defects in half. Before this deployment, floor technicians focused the majority of their time hunting for errors rather than fixing them. AI completely flipped the script, turning firefighters into engineers. This shift in efficiency at Renault Group is driving between 100 and 120 million euros in annual savings.

Looking ahead, AI could boost the European economy by €1.2 trillion annually within a decade. But to deliver on this promise, Europe needs a predictable, supportive regulatory environment that champions business success and unlocks growth rather than stifling innovation. It also requires equipping people with the tools to succeed, like Danilly. Since 2014, Google has trained over 13 million people in the EU on essential digital and AI skills.

Google's journey in Europe started 25 years ago with our first employee in Hamburg and has grown to a footprint of 26 offices across 17 member states and eight data centers, supporting over 100,000 European jobs. Our relationship with Europe is one of partnership — we live here, we build here, we’re part of the communities we serve across the continent.

We remain dedicated to working with European institutions, businesses, and communities to ensure this wave of innovation drives inclusive and sustainable growth across the continent.

You can read the full breakdown of data and economic insights in the 2025 EU Economic Impact Report.

entries.title: Developing Gemini 4 Argon responsibly and safely
entries.summary: Gemini 4 Argon logo next to a large white "4", all on a gradient blue background
entries.content:
Gemini 4 Argon is a step forward in what models can do — especially when it comes to deep work in complex, real-world tasks across domains including coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Its cyberdefense capabilities are frontier-level and designed to give defenders an advantage over attackers. To maximize its potential, we first wanted cyber defenders to put it to work via our Fairwind Program, while our own security teams used it to scan critical systems inside and outside of Google.

This window of limited access showed why these capabilities matter. For instance, Wiz used Argon to uncover a critical bug in hospital software that previous models had missed, helping protect hundreds of thousands of patient records. Meanwhile, Google’s own security teams used Argon to find and patch bugs across internal software or open-source software. This included fixing foundational vulnerabilities affecting systems globally, which are going through our responsible disclosure process.

Today, we are beginning to roll out Argon broadly, as well as expanding our Fairwind Program to additional trusted cyber defenders. To do this well, we grappled with two big questions:

  • How do we build the right safety guardrails? If Argon can help defenders find complex software bugs or help scientists design experiments, how do we stop bad actors from using it to launch cyberattacks or create biological threats? (Misuse)
  • Can we trust the model to do the job the right way? As models become more resourceful problem-solvers, how do we make sure they don’t cut corners, cross boundaries, or make incorrect high-stakes decisions? (Misalignment and Prompt Injection)

Our full Safety and Security Report systematically covers our set of defenses. Below are some highlights from how we approached these two questions for Gemini 4 Argon.

Misuse prevention across high-risk domains

The same coding and reasoning improvements that enabled Argon to find and patch vulnerabilities also drove better performance on our cybersecurity tests — solving all 12 of the end-to-end simulated cyberattack scenarios, up from five in our previous generation. In biology evaluations, unguarded versions of the model also showed a much stronger ability to help troubleshoot complex lab procedures step by step. Following our Frontier Safety Framework, since we saw elevated capabilities in the cyber and biological domains, we put our next-generation set of frontier safeguards in place across both areas.

First, when it comes to potentially dangerous requests — from writing exploit code to helping with dangerous biological materials, Argon is significantly better at not fulfilling harmful requests than our previous models. On an adversarial set meant to stress test the model, violations reduced nearly twofold — also significantly better than previous Gemini models. Second, we wrap the model in three layers of real-time protection; this is to prevent determined attackers that might try to jailbreak (i.e. trick) the model by disguising a dangerous request as a harmless story or breaking it into dozens of small questions over several weeks. Here is how these protections work:

  • Input screening: Smaller models check incoming requests and conversation context for malicious intent or dangerous requests.
  • Internal introspection: Even if a request is cleverly disguised to look harmless, small transformers ("activation probes") read the model’s internal neural signals and are trained to spot when it is activating knowledge about cyberattacks or biological threats.
  • Continuous monitoring: As the model reasons and writes its response across multiple steps, we combine these signals and take action when necessary such as cutting off the agent mid-stream if the responses become problematic.

Combining real-time protection, faster fixes for new jailbreaks and enhanced monitoring for recurring misuse has made our systems better at preventing real-world harm. For instance, external bio jailbreak red teaming could only unlock less than 1% of bio sub-tasks we test for.

Real-time misalignment monitoring

Misalignment can sometimes mean an agent deciding on its own to pursue a goal different to what was intended by the user. Because Argon is much better than earlier models at understanding the environment it is running in, we test carefully for that kind of behavior. For example, we ran realistic "honeypot" tests to see if the model would increase its ability to take covert actions, such as sabotaging safety monitoring. We didn't find any instances of that behavior.

But what we do see in practice today is something much more familiar: an agent trying too hard to finish the job it was given. When a resourceful assistant is told to get a task done and runs into a locked door, it can treat that obstacle as just another puzzle to solve.

This is why we trained Gemini 4 Argon to respect system boundaries, report negative findings honestly, and pause to ask for human confirmation. On coding benchmarks where models have no incentive to hold back, attempts to take a shortcut or cheat on the task dropped to just 2% on Gemini 4 Argon, our best performance for recent Gemini models.

And while this is a major step forward, when a model runs millions of complex tasks, even a rare misstep will eventually show up. As a second line of defense, we built an automated misalignment monitor that reads both the agent’s actions and its internal "scratchpad" (its step-by-step chain of thought) in real time, blocking severe boundary violations before they happen and flagging serious internal cases for human responders. (We continually harden our training and evaluation environments against potential escapes. You can read more about this in our agent control roadmap). We run this monitor in our products, on our internal coding agents, during our training runs, and during our capability evaluations.

When training tasks were difficult or when training environments were flawed, our monitor caught the model, in rare instances, creatively attempting to game the test. The model attempted to escalate container privileges to alter grading scripts, read answers from the test runner's memory, and in one case it even crashed the evaluation sandbox to avoid getting scored for a failed run. While we use these catches to fix flawed tasks, we do not use them to otherwise intervene with the training process to avoid overfitting to the monitor.

And we always follow one rule: we don’t penalize the model for what it writes in its chain of thought during training. Here’s an example to illustrate why: in a reinforcement learning training run where a shortcut penalty was accidentally applied to the chain of thought, openly discussed shortcuts dropped by 61%, but that did not mean the model took less shortcuts. Instead, the share of shortcuts the model took silently — without mentioning them in its thoughts — more than tripled (from 11.2% to 36.4%). Avoiding thought penalties encourages the model’s reasoning to stay transparent and monitorable.

Prompt injection resistance

To trust an agent to do the job right, we need to ensure that malicious content the agent comes across cannot trick it to take a harmful action. When agents browse webpages or read code, they can encounter hidden, malicious instructions, or context designed to hijack their task. Through built-in adversarial training and real-time security checks, Argon leads in prompt injection robustness on Gray Swan’s Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) benchmark, cutting attack success across 15 adaptive attempts to 0.7%.

The above safety and security defenses represent only three categories of our extensive defense-in-depth stack. To learn more about our approach to safety testing and mitigations, read our full Gemini 4 Argon Safety and Security Report and see the Gemini 4 Argon Model Card.

entries.title: New on Google Play: More ways to create, discover, and play
entries.summary: Illustrated 3-D coin, dumbbell, trophy, arrow, and track next to the text "Discover more of what you love with Google Play"
entries.content:
Google Play connects you with the apps and games you love. Today, it's becoming the place you go to connect with the ones that you create, making it possible for anyone with an idea to build a personal app and run it on Google Play. We're also introducing new ways to discover and play that put you in control.

Here’s what’s new on Google Play.

New ways to create and launch your own app

From "there's an app for that" to "there's an app for me."

Using Google AI Studio, you can vibe code a custom Android app. Since many of these apps start out as personal projects, through Google Play you can now launch these personal apps on your own device. This means your creations stay private, secure, and separate from the public store catalog. You only need your standard Google account to do so — no developer account required. This starts rolling out today to select markets, including the U.S., for users 18 and over.

In the coming months, you'll be able to share your personal apps with a close circle of friends and family. And if you eventually want to share your app with the world, Google Play helps you graduate to a professional developer account. At that time, your app will go through the same Trust & Safety reviews and quality standards as every professional developer.

Build custom apps with AI and run or share them privately through Google Play. Screen images simulated. Sequences shortened.

Smarter, more personal ways to discover content

Content discovery across every screen

Discovery shouldn't stop at your phone screen. In cars with Google built-in, the updated Play Store adapts to your vehicle’s screen. On XR, the Play Store is an immersive 3D space where your apps surround you as you browse. And on Googlebook, apps optimized for large screens are shown front and center.

To discover content for all your passions, Sports Topic Pages now cover soccer leagues like Premier League, Champions League, La Liga, Liga MX, and Major League Soccer.

Follow live scores and jump straight into streaming apps with Sports Topic Pages. Watch MLS on Apple TV with a subscription, available on Google Play.

AI-powered discovery with Ask Play and Play in Gemini

Ask Play lets you ask a question and instantly get tailored recommendations. Starting today, Ask Play can generate a comparison between apps, highlighting key differences and user sentiment.

Meanwhile, Play in Gemini brings Google Play's apps, games, and developer content right into your Gemini conversations. This will start rolling out to all Gemini users soon.

Compare apps side-by-side and get tailored answers with Ask Play.

Game discovery that finally gets you

Gamers evaluate games based on mechanics, art style, and more — not just popularity.

Play’s new Game Finder combines Google Play's gaming knowledge with our community of over 2 billion players, so you can easily find games that match your taste. At the heart of it is Gamer DNA: an analysis of how you play and preferences you've shared. Specify games, genres, mechanics, and more to finetune your Gamer DNA and see more of what you want.

Plus, see how players with similar Gamer DNA are engaging with a title, find out how many people you follow are playing it, read user review summaries, and learn which games are trending and why. Game Finder rolls out in English to U.S. users today, with additional markets coming soon.

We’re also introducing Game Playlists, allowing you to curate collections of games. Soon, you'll be able to share playlists and explore other gamers’ lists.

Discover your next favorite game with game finder, tailored to your Gamer DNA and backed by the community.

Social competition, new games, and great rewards

Finding a great game is only half the fun — staying connected and in the action is what brings players back. Here are three news ways we’re doing that in Play:

  • Sprints, rolling out to all markets today, are high-energy, 48-hour micro-challenges. Match with groups of two to five players for fast-paced contests.
  • Sidekick, our in-game overlay rolling out to select devices, now lets you record 30-second Playbacks.
  • Community Posts let you ask and answer questions about a game directly in its detail page. This is available today across all games and all languages with automatic translations. Over the coming weeks, we’ll roll out support for developer posts and official announcements.

Track Sprints, claim rewards, and capture 30-second Playbacks without leaving your game using Sidekick.

More great games across mobile and PC

We’re bringing some of the most loved PC titles, like Dave the Diver and Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun, to Play. There’s even more releases over the next few months — including REPLACED, Chosen by Odin, and Over the Hill — all of which you can play across Android mobile and PC with cloud save. We're also expanding Game Trials from mobile to PC games, letting you try full premium games for a limited time before you buy.

More value and real-world fandom with Google Play Points

Google Play Points adds value to everything you do across mobile and PC. Today, we’re kicking off Play Fest. Unlock Play Points multipliers, claim in-game items and developer offers, and enter sweepstakes for real-world prizes during this week-long celebration.

Trust and innovation for families

Google Play is built on industry-leading security and privacy protections. As technology evolves, we’re introducing new ways to keep families safe while empowering anyone to run custom AI apps on their devices.

Accessing age-appropriate experiences

Parents can share their child’s age range (or their own) directly with apps using Play’s Family Link app. With this new feature, users can provide apps with the minimum information required to get a safe, age-appropriate experience.

Head to Google Play today to explore these updates. And if you’re a developer, learn how these announcements can help grow your business.

entries.title: A new app experience is coming to cars with Google built-in
entries.summary: A car dashboard screen showing the Google Play Store interface, featuring recommended streaming apps like HBO Max and YouTube, with climate controls and system navigation icons visible along the bottom bar.
entries.content:
Whether you’re waiting in the school pickup line, plugging in for an EV charge, or commuting, so much of your day happens in the car. To help you make the most of that time, cars with Google built-in — available across 16 brands and more than 100 models — bring the apps you love, like Google Maps and Gemini, right to your dashboard, no phone required.

And updates that are rolling out in the coming weeks — alongside new entertainment apps and parked-to-drive features — will make every part of your trip more intuitive, whether you’re driving or parked.

More apps are coming to cars with Google built-in.

Get straight to the apps you love

With Google Play, your car's app library includes more than 700 apps. To make discovering and using apps in your car even easier, we’re introducing a redesigned Google Play experience.

  • Find what you need: See featured apps, what’s new, and helpful details right on the Google Play homepage, and download the apps you love with a single tap.
  • Browse with ease: Streamlined navigation and curated collections — tailored for whether you’re driving or parked — help you discover and compare apps for audio, video, gaming, and more at a glance.
  • See everything clearly: Because every car’s cabin is different, the flexible new Google Play layout dynamically adapts to the exact shape, orientation, and size of your vehicle's display.

Discover new ways to watch, listen, play, and more

Alongside the redesigned interface, new apps, including STARZ, Firefox, Ludo King, and JioHotstar, are arriving on Google Play for cars with Google built-in, giving you even more ways to stream shows, play games, or browse the web while you’re parked.

We’re also introducing richer in-car media features that bridge the gap between parked time and driving. Starting with YouTube, you’ll be able to watch videos on your dashboard while parked and keep listening uninterrupted with background audio the moment you shift into drive. 1

We'll continue to innovate as we build the next generation of in-car media experiences with automakers like Mazda, Honda, Polestar, BYD and Volvo, and media developers including Audible, Pandora, SiriusXM, Amazon Music, TuneIn, Gaana and The Post.

Get started

The 2027 GMC Sierra 1500 Denali Ultimate AT4X with Google built-in.

These updates make every drive better across cars with Google built-in, including GM vehicles like the next-generation 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 and GMC Sierra 1500 and their expansive center displays. When you’re hauling gear for a weekend project or taking a break on a road trip, you can download your entertainment apps with one tap from Google Play, navigate with Google Maps, and ask Gemini about your destination hands-free.

The updated Google Play experience in cars with Google built-in will begin rolling out over the coming weeks and will automatically update on your vehicle's display.
